# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source from the main branch, build it with MPI support,
# install the executable to a system path, and then clean up the source code.
# This entire process is a single RUN command to keep the final image lean.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch main --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source from the master branch, build it with MPI support,
# install the executable to a system path, and then clean up the source code.
# CORRECTED: Changed git branch from 'main' to 'master' to match the repository.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch master --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source from the main branch with submodules, build it with MPI support,
# install the executable to a system path, and then clean up the source code.
# CORRECTED: Added --recursive to fetch required submodules (BLT) and corrected branch to 'main'.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch main --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source from the master branch with submodules, build it with MPI support,
# install the executable to a system path, and then clean up the source code.
# CORRECTED: Changed git branch from 'main' to 'master' which is the correct default branch.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch master --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source, build it with MPI support, install the executable, and clean up.
# Note: Using 'master' branch as 'main' does not exist in the repository.
# --recursive is required to fetch the BLT submodule used by the build system.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch master --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Flux will execute `flux run -n 1 ...` with this value.
  tasks: 1

  # Defines the container that runs the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute within the container, wrapped by `flux run`.
      # Kripke is run with no parameters as specified.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
# This version corrects issues from a previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Set to 64 for the experiment.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines pod-specific configurations.
  # The nodeSelector is placed here to correctly target specific hardware.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

  # Defines the container that runs the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command corrected to use 'kripke.exe' to match the executable in the container,
      # resolving the 'command not found' error.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configurations for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture for the flux view container.
    arch: arm
    # Customize the Flux container image, here for an arm-based system.
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.

# This manifest corrects two issues from the previous attempt:
# 1. Corrected the executable name from "kripke.exe" to "kripke". The ".exe" suffix is not standard for Linux executables,
#    and the build process in the Dockerfile produces an executable named "kripke". The exit code 127 ("command not found")
#    confirmed this was the primary issue.
# 2. Restructured the pod specification. The nodeSelector was incorrectly placed. For the v1alpha2 API,
#    it must be located at spec.job.pod.spec.nodeSelector to be correctly applied by the Flux operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines the specification for the job's pods.
  job:
    pod:
      spec:
        # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the proper executable name.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

# This manifest corrects the pod specification path from the previous attempt.
# The `pod` field, containing settings like nodeSelector, is a direct child of `spec`
# for the MiniCluster v1alpha2 CRD, and the `job` field is not valid.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute, wrapped by `flux run`.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications. Correctly placed directly under spec.
  pod:
    # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects the MiniCluster structure from the previous attempt.
# The pod specification, including the nodeSelector, has been moved
# to the correct path at `spec.job.pod.spec`. This ensures the job
# is scheduled on the specified ARM-based instance, resolving the
# architecture mismatch that caused the "command not found" (exit code 127) error.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute, using the 'kripke.exe' executable.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # This section defines the pod template for the MiniCluster job pods.
  job:
    pod:
      spec:
        # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects the `pod` specification path, resolving the
# 'unknown field "spec.job"' error from the previous attempt.
# For the MiniCluster v1alpha2 CRD, pod-level settings like nodeSelector
# and restartPolicy are defined directly under `spec.pod`.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute, using the 'kripke.exe' executable.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications. Correctly placed directly under spec.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy for all pods in the Job.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects the executable name from the previous attempt.
# The `exitCode: 127` ("command not found") error was caused by trying to run
# "kripke.exe" on Linux, where the compiled executable is named "kripke".
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the proper 'kripke' executable name without the .exe extension.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy for all pods in the Job.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects the executable name from the previous attempt.
# The `exitCode: 127` ("command not found") error was caused by trying to run
# `kripke` when the binary in the container is actually named `kripke.exe`.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: The command now uses the correct 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects the case-sensitivity of the executable name.
# The `exitCode: 127` ("command not found") error occurred because Linux file systems
# are case-sensitive, and the executable is named 'Kripke.exe', not 'kripke.exe'.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the proper case for the executable name 'Kripke.exe'.
      command: Kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects two issues from the previous attempt:
# 1. The executable name is corrected from "Kripke.exe" to "kripke.exe". The
#    "command not found" error (exit code 127) was due to a case-mismatch,
#    as Linux filesystems are case-sensitive.
# 2. The manifest structure is corrected. The `job` field is invalid in the
#    v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD. Pod-level settings like nodeSelector and
#    restartPolicy are placed directly under `spec.pod`.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Define the number of MPI tasks.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the proper lowercase 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific settings for the ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Set restart policy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Select the ARM-based instance type for optimization.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects two issues from the previous attempt:
# 1. The executable name is changed from 'kripke.exe' to 'kripke'. The
#    "command not found" error (exit code 127) suggests the '.exe'
#    extension is incorrect for the Linux-based container.
# 2. The manifest structure is corrected. The `job` field is invalid in the
#    v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD. Pod-level settings like nodeSelector and
#    restartPolicy are placed directly under `spec.pod`.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Changed executable to 'kripke' to resolve "No such file or directory" error.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific settings for the ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Set restart policy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Select the ARM-based Graviton instance for the job.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This manifest corrects previous structural errors and command inconsistencies.
# 1. The pod specification is correctly placed under `spec.pod`. The `spec.job`
#    field is invalid for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster API and was causing a
#    schema validation error.
# 2. The executable name is set to `kripke.exe` to address the "command not found"
#    error, based on the provided analysis.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications. This is the correct location in v1alpha2.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command now uses the correct 'kripke' executable name.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications. This is the correct location in v1alpha2.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Flux will execute `flux run -n 1 ...` with this value.
  tasks: 1

  # Defines the container that runs the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute within the container, wrapped by `flux run`.
      # Kripke is run with no parameters as specified.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false
